<Rep. Maxine Waters, Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, Rep. Stephen F. Lynch, Rep. Al Green, Rep. Emanuel Cleaver, Rep. Bill Foster, Rep. Joyce Beatty, Rep. Juan Vargas, Rep. Rashida Tlaib, Rep. Sylvia R. Garcia, Rep. Nikema Williams>: This bill would modify the bank merger review process and force the Federal Reserve, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to either approve or deny a merger application within 90 days of receiving an initial application, even if the application is not complete and the merging parties have not provided all the information regulators request to adequately assess the merger application. Additionally, the bill would limit regulators' ability to consider feedback from affected stakeholders on proposed mergers. These reforms will bring less scrutiny, not more, to a rubber-stamping process that has wiped out community banks and significantly increased the market share the largest banks have.
Experts have argued that the bank merger review process has been too lax and has amounted to a rubber-stamping process, resulting in banking deserts and too-big-to manage banks that have compliance challenges, consumer harm, or higher prices for financial products and services.\1\ These concerns came into focus in the context of the merger of Capital One and Discover to form the 6th largest commercial bank and the largest credit card loan company.\2\ Ranking Member Waters and others have raised concerns,\3\ but the Trump Administration recently approved the merger.\4\
\1\See Jeremy Kress, Modernizing Bank Merger Review, Yale Journal on Regulation (Aug. 17, 2021); Comment Letter from Jeremy Kress to FDIC regarding comments on FDIC Policy on Bank Merger Transactions (May 31, 2022); Better Markets, Fact Sheet: The Review Process for Bank Mergers and Acquisitions is Seriously Deficient, Allows Too-Big-To-Fail To Proliferate, and Fails to Protect Consumers (Jul. 11, 2023); and Better Markets, Bank Mergers Require Robust Scrutiny to Ensure that Consumers' Interests Are Not Sacrificed for Wall Street's Profits (May 12, 2025).
\2\See FSC, Maxine Waters, Ranking Member, Opposes Capital One's Proposed Purchase of Discover (Feb. 21, 2024).
\3\FSC, Waters Testifies Against Proposed Capital One-Discover Merger at Regulators' Public Meeting (Jul. 19, 2024).
\4\FSC, Ranking Member Maxine Waters Slams Trump Administration's Approval of Capital One-Discover Merger (Apr. 21, 2025).
Experts cite to overwhelming approval rates for mergers; for example, the Fed indicated that between 2006 and 2017, it approved 3,316 merger applications, and while other applications were withdrawn, the agency formally denied zero applications during that time.\5\ Even when accounting for withdrawn applications, the approval rate has been extremely high; in 2021 and 2022, the Fed approved roughly 97% and 94% of merger applications, respectively, even when factoring in withdrawn applications.\6\ The last time bank regulators denied a merger application was 2003.\7\
\5\See Sen. Elizabeth Warren, Letter from Fed Chair Powell to Sen. Warren (May 10, 2018).
\6\Fed, Banking Applications Activity Semiannual Report, July- December 2023 (Apr. 2024). Also see Fed, Semiannual Reports on Banking Applications Activity (accessed Apr. 27, 2024).
\7\Jeremy Kress, Modernizing Bank Merger Review, Yale Journal on Regulation (Aug. 17, 2021).
In an attempt to address these concerns, former President Biden issued an Executive Order encouraging regulators to promote market competition, including directing the Department of Justice (DOJ) to consult with Federal banking regulators to review and strengthen their bank merger review policies.\8\ Ranking Member Waters and Committee Democrats called on regulators to take prompt action to strengthen merger review procedures,\9\ for example, by holding public hearings with large bank mergers to ensure affected workers, consumers, and small business owners have ample opportunity to express their views. While the FDIC, OCC, and Department of Justice under the Biden Administration made some reforms to strengthen their bank merger reviews last year (the Fed never did), Trump's regulators have begun to roll back many of these merger review reforms.\10\
\8\White House, Executive Order on Promoting Competition in the American Economy, EO 14036 (Jul. 9, 2021).
\9\FSC, Ranking Member Waters Leads 15 Committee Democrats in Urging Banking Regulators to Quickly Revamp Bank Merger Review Procedures Following Proposed Capital One Merger with Discover (Feb. 28, 2024).
\10\Consumer Finance Monitor, FDIC proposing rescinding merger policy adopted in September (Mar. 10, 2025).
This bill was previously included in H.R. 8337 (118th), Bank Resilience and Regulatory Improvement Act, which passed FSC last year by a 24-22 partisan vote, though it was never considered by the full House. When this was considered last Congress, some consumer groups warned, ``The bank merger review process is supposed to protect Americans against the dangers of bank consolidation and bank mergers that are not in the interest of customers or for which managerial resources are lacking . . . We oppose the bill as it would dangerously require the agencies to decide on merger applications even when the application is not complete and/or the merging parties have not provided all the information regulators request to adequately assess the merger application. Regulators have a consistent pattern of waving mergers through without sufficient scrutiny--creating an increasingly consolidated market that makes banking more expensive for consumers and increases systemic risk. Merger scrutiny needs to become more robust, not less so, as this bill would require.''\11\
\11\AFR et al, Letter to FSC (May 16, 2024).
A number of consumer and community groups oppose the bill, including Americans for Financial Reform (AFR), Center for Responsible Lending (CRL), Consumer Federation of America (CFA), Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy, National Consumer Law Center, on behalf of its low-income clients (NCLC), National Community Reinvestment Coalition (NCRC), New Economy Project, Public Citizen, Rise Economy, and 20/20 Vision.
For these reasons, we oppose H.R. 1900.
Sincerely,
Maxine Waters,
Ranking Member.
Nydia M. Velazquez,
Stephen F. Lynch,
Al Green,
Emanuel Cleaver, II,
Bill Foster,
Joyce Beatty,
Juan Vargas,
Rashida Tlaib,
Sylvia R. Garcia,
Nikema Williams,
Members of Congress.
